transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maria Torres (Acme Health - Head of ML), James Li (Platform Eng), Nora Patel (Security), Keenan O'Rourke (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): final rollout planning, canary thresholds, monitoring dashboards, security sign-off pending.

00:00 Alex Chen: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining our weekly POC sync. quick check-in, we have 38 minutes, want to focus on rollout and go-live planning today, canary and runbooks.
00:12 Maria Torres: yes thanks Alex, excited — we've got execs asking for dates so we need to lock the cutover plan this week.
00:18 Priya Nair: hi team, quick context: from the last run we saw stable latencies on Redwood Dedicated at our target 512 token average but we need to validate autoscaling behavior under burst.
00:30 James Li: right, the main unknown for us is how the KV cache reacts when we switch to live traffic patterns. sometimes we saw cold-start thumps and a small latency spike.
00:42 Priya Nair: yeah we observed a 150-200ms tail in one of the runs, probably due to cold KV cache on a few pods. we have suggestions: prefix caching and a staggered pre-warm during canary.
00:55 Nora Patel: on security side, SOC2 doc is good, but we need explicit KMS/HSM confirmation and audit log retention for 365 days, also SSO/SAML test plan.
01:05 Alex Chen: noted, Nora. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs in the control plane; I'll send the security addendum and KMS config notes.
01:15 Maria Torres: timeline: we'd like to cutover end of month, ideally 2026-11-30, but that depends on the canary results and sign-offs.
01:25 Keenan O'Rourke: product would prefer a two-week gradual ramp after canary to monitor real-world QA, A/B testing the new model with 10% traffic.
01:37 Priya Nair: proposed canary plan: 1% for 1 hour, 5% for 4 hours, 20% for 24 hours, then A/B at 10% for 48 hours before full cut. we can shorten steps if metrics look good.
01:50 James Li: sounds reasonable. what metrics are we going to watch? latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost per request, and a small quality sample set for prompt regression.
02:02 Priya Nair: yes, we'll push dashboards: latency histograms, infra GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, token cost estimates per minute, and also a fraud/error spike alert.
02:15 Nora Patel: alerting — we need escalation paths and runbook owner names. in particular, if latency p99 exceeds 1200ms for more than 5 minutes, auto-fallback to hosted model variant must be triggered. do you support automatic fallback?
02:28 Alex Chen: yes, Redwood routing supports fallback policies by model variant and region. we can wire an automatic fallback to the lighter quantized variant or to Hosted API to preserve availability. we'll document it in the runbook.
02:40 Maria Torres: good. can we do a dry-run of the runbook with our ops on Friday?
02:45 Alex Chen: absolutely. Priya, can you run the dry-run script?
02:48 Priya Nair: yep I can lead the tabletop and a simulated canary. I'll share the draft runbook link after the call.
02:55 James Li: on A/B testing, we need a control and treatment split; control stays on current model, treatment on new Redwood variant. we want to measure latency, TPU/GPU cost, and an NPS-like quality metric from our manual evals.
03:10 Keenan O'Rourke: for product sign-off, we'll require no more than 3% regression on critical prompts and no increase in error rate.
03:20 Maria Torres: also need to confirm data residency — some PHI flows go to EU region. can Redwood ensure routing to eu-west-1 for those customers?
03:29 Alex Chen: yes, routing by region is supported, and we can pin model instances to eu-west-1. for Private deployments we can also do on-prem for specific tenants if required.
03:40 Nora Patel: KMS question again — does Redwood Private let us use our HSM-backed keys? we can't hand over plaintext keys to a vendor.
03:49 Priya Nair: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; Priya: sorry I mean Redwood supports that. you can keep keys in your KMS and we encrypt at rest with those keys; we'll share the integration doc.
04:00 Maria Torres: ok good. next, what's the rollback plan if we see quality regressions during A/B?
04:08 Priya Nair: rollback is: immediate traffic shift back to control using routing policies, revoke any new model rollouts, and then run the postmortem. runbook includes a traffic-shift command and a checklist: notify stakeholders, capture request traces, export sample prompts for eval.
04:25 James Li: for monitoring, can you push Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards or do we need Redwood Console access?
04:32 Alex Chen: we can do both. Redwood Console will have per-route dashboards; we can stream metrics to your Prometheus endpoint as well or export via our metrics API.
04:45 Keenan O'Rourke: who owns the canary monitoring during business hours? ops or Redwood?
04:50 Maria Torres: we want joint ownership. ops handles on-call, Redwood provides escalation for model/runtime issues.
04:58 Priya Nair: noted. we'll add an escalation matrix in runbook.
05:05 Nora Patel: legal/procurement timeline — do we need a signed SLA before cutover? procurement expects a 2-week lead for signatures.
05:13 Alex Chen: we can fast-track SLA approvals; I'll loop in sales legal. could push a draft today.
05:20 Maria Torres: another question — pricing forecast during canary. we can't exceed our budget while testing. any recommendations?
05:27 Alex Chen: we can cap burst and apply a temporary cost cap on dedicated pool; also enable autoscaling limits so you don't blow past targets. I'll include examples in pricing doc.
05:38 Priya Nair: last technical note: pre-warm pods by issuing synthetic requests that mirror top prompt prefixes, that reduces KV cold misses. we'll provide a pre-warm script.
05:50 James Li: ok let's confirm dates: runbenchmarks 11/24-11/25, draft runbook by 11/23, dry-run tabletop 11/26, final cutover target 11/30 but Maria to confirm.
06:05 Maria Torres: yes I should have final decision by 11/24 after internal exec review.
06:12 Alex Chen: recap of next steps: Alex send security & pricing docs, Priya send canary runbook + pre-warm script, Priya to schedule benchmark window, James to give traffic ramp specs, Nora to confirm KMS requirements.
06:30 Keenan O'Rourke: sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:35 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in slack and CRM. meeting adjourned.
